results.title: The statement 22P_AP: long progressions of good slope primes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement 22P_AP is the assertion that for every $K\in\mathbb N$ there are integers $x\ge1$ and $v\ge1$ such that each of the $K+1$ numbers is a good slope prime larger than every prime of $S_b=S_{\rm ht}\cup\mathcal H$.

results.title: A slope with prime numerators satisfies field 2′
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $u,v\in\mathbb Z$ with $v>0$. Suppose that for each $b\in\mathcal C\cup\{1\}$ the number $|u-bv|$ is a prime larger than every prime of $S_b$, that for each $b\in\mathcal C$ it is a good slope prime, and that $F(u/v)>0$. Then $t=u/v$ satisfies conditions 1, 2′, 3, 4 for $B_0=0$.

results.title: Proposition AP: progressions of good slope primes give the slope representation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Assume 22P_AP. Then the slope representation under field 2′ holds: every integer $A$ is a sum of three rationals satisfying conditions 1, 2′, 3, 4 for $B_0=0$.

results.title: 22P_AP from Green–Tao and Proposition D
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Assume Szemerédi's theorem in the primes (every set of primes of positive relative upper density contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length) and that the good slope primes have positive relative upper density in the primes. Then 22P_AP holds.
